author: jsign
content:
> I don't agree with the lack of tick against "The team maintaining the guest program must be considered sustainable". Erigontech (and associated people) have been maintaining Erigon and other core Ethereum software and EIPs for like 7 years now. I would consider that sufficient for this criterion. We are also confident in our sub-team within Erigontech to maintain Zilkworm for a long time.
Yep, I agree with <@976542403269910539>  the sustainability condition can be considered satisfied by Zilkworm given that is backed by the Erigon team. 👍 

> ELF files and artifacts will be published in future in more places too. Currently it's already in https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/releases
Nice. Are you currently working on potentially doing a release compliatn with tests-zkevm@v0.8.x? (mainly[ v0.8.0](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/releases/tag/tests-zkevm%40v0.8.0) has bulk of spec changes, there is a newer v0.8.2 that has some extra stuff but doesn't change anything spec relevant). 
If this is possible, we could add Zilkworm in ere-guest via the [artifacts-registry.json](https://github.com/eth-act/ere-guests/blob/main/artifact-registry.json)... which I think would be awesome.
Would be easy to add, and include in all our testing and benchmarking pipelines. (But note we are only considering ELFs that expect input and output compliant with tests-zkevm@v0.8.x).

> We may reconsider the MIT licensing in future, but for now we will stick to Apache 2.0 on Zilkworm and associated repos.
Do you think might be a big lift for Zilkworm to also include MIT? 
Etherex, Reth, and Zesu are MIT+Apache2.0, and Nethermind is doing some work trying to switch to the dual license... so would be ideal if Zilkworm wasn't an exception.

author: somnergy
content:
> Nice. Are you currently working on potentially doing a release compliatn with tests-zkevm@v0.8.x? 
Yes, currently we are working on direct compatibility as well as adapted input bytes for our flat-state scheme. Both would be released soon. We are treating it as a priority this month. (You must already know that we have worked on a flat-witness scheme yet to be released)

> Do you think might be a big lift for Zilkworm to also include MIT?
I guess I haven't dived into it yet. I think Zilkworm has potential beyond just the guest program down the line for Ethereum proofs, hence the added burden for the right call.

author: jsign
content: Thanks <@976542403269910539>! Please keep me updated on those two fronts whenever you have any updates 🙏

author: developeruche
content: Do you have numbers for the flat-state scheme already? do you mind sharing 🙂 🙏

author: developeruche
content: Just so we on the same page... in conclusion, Zilkworm main repo would in the future publish it ELF to `ere-guest` and it input format would be spec comp (SSZ - this could be optionally presented to allow other input format Zilkworm is experimenting), this would in turn make `zilkworm-stateless` redundant and no reason for a repo transfer anymore.

author: somnergy
content: I don't yet, we re-designed the state for flat witness scheme, and now I am working on optimizing a version that would run off of statelessInputBytes ssz without relying on any superpowers. But the latter must be optimized as much as possible too, for fair game.

author: developeruche
content: Alright... would be looking out for this

author: somnergy
content: Thank you for being patient so far
